title: Creativity, insight and “eureka moments,” with John Kounios, PhD

sentences.en: Have you ever worked on a problem for hours or days or even weeks, turning it over in your mind until you were ready to give up finding a solution?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾为解决一个问题苦思冥想了数小时、数天甚至数周，直到你准备放弃寻找答案？

sentences.en: But then the answer came to you in a flash, maybe in the shower or while you were taking a walk or doing the dishes.
sentences.zh: 但随后答案却突然闪现在你脑海中，也许是在洗澡时，或者是在散步、洗碗的时候。

sentences.en: Many of us are fortunate enough to experience these spurts of insight at least occasionally.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人都有幸至少偶尔能体验到这种灵光一现的时刻。

sentences.en: Aha or Eureka moments have led to some of humanity's greatest achievements in science, medicine, mathematics, and art, from classic songs to life-saving cancer treatments, even
sentences.zh: “啊哈”或“尤里卡”时刻促成了人类在科学、医学、数学和艺术领域的一些最伟大的成就，从经典歌曲到挽救生命的癌症治疗，甚至

sentences.en: to the invention of the slinky.
sentences.zh: 包括弹簧玩具的发明。

sentences.en: But most of the time, these insights are more prosaic.
sentences.zh: 但大多数时候，这些灵感更为平淡。

sentences.en: Maybe a crossword puzzle answer that's eluded you for days comes to your mind in the shower
sentences.zh: 也许是一个困扰了你几天的填字游戏答案在洗澡时突然浮现，

sentences.en: or the perfect title for a paper you're writing pops into your head while you're digging a hole in the garden.
sentences.zh: 又或者是在花园里挖坑时，你正在写的论文的完美标题突然蹦进了脑海。

sentences.en: Eureka moments like these are a form of creativity.
sentences.zh: 像这样的“尤里卡”时刻是一种创造力的表现。

sentences.en: They involve coming up with a new idea or a novel solution to a problem.
sentences.zh: 它们涉及想出一个新点子或解决问题的新颖方案。

sentences.en: So how does this type of creative insight differ from more analytical or methodical thinking?
sentences.zh: 那么，这种创造性洞察与更具分析性或条理性的思维有何不同？

sentences.en: Where in the brain does creative insight happen?
sentences.zh: 创造性洞察发生在大脑的什么位置？

sentences.en: Are some people naturally more creative thinkers than others?
sentences.zh: 有些人天生比其他人更具创造性思维吗？

sentences.en: And how can you encourage more creativity in yourself and set yourself up to experience more of these aha moments?
sentences.zh: 你该如何激发自己的创造力，并让自己更容易体验到这些“啊哈”时刻？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. John Kunios, a professor of psychology at Drexel University in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是费城德雷塞尔大学的心理学教授约翰·库尼奥斯博士。

sentences.en: Two decades ago, his work provided some of the first evidence from brain imaging studies that creative insight is a distinct form of thinking separate from analytical thought.
sentences.zh: 二十年前，他的研究提供了脑成像研究中首批证据，表明创造性洞察是一种独立于分析思维的独特思维形式。

sentences.en: Since then, he has continued to study what's happening in people's brains during moments of creativity and insight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他一直致力于研究人们在创造力和洞察力迸发时大脑中发生的变化。

sentences.en: He is also author of the book, The Eureka Factor, Aha Moments, Creative Insight, and the Brain.
sentences.zh: 他也是《尤里卡因素：啊哈时刻、创造性洞察与大脑》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Kunios.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天参加我们的节目，库尼奥斯博士。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for inviting me.
sentences.zh: 感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: So a moment ago, I said that aha moments or eureka moments are a form of creative thinking.
sentences.zh: 刚才我说过，“啊哈”时刻或“尤里卡”时刻是一种创造性思维形式。

sentences.en: Let's talk about that a little more.
sentences.zh: 让我们再深入探讨一下。

sentences.en: A lot of people think of creativity more in terms of things like musical or artistic ability.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为创造力更多是指音乐或艺术能力之类的东西。

sentences.en: What makes an aha moment a type of creativity?
sentences.zh: 是什么让“啊哈”时刻成为一种创造力？

sentences.en: Okay, well, let's first start with what creativity is.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们先从什么是创造力开始说起。

sentences.en: Creativity is not just in the arts.
sentences.zh: 创造力不仅仅存在于艺术中。

sentences.en: Creativity occurs in science.
sentences.zh: 创造力也出现在科学中。

sentences.en: Creativity occurs in everyday life, in all aspects of life.
sentences.zh: 创造力出现在日常生活中，出现在生活的方方面面。

sentences.en: So probably the most common definition is that for something to be creative, it involves coming up with an idea or a product that is both novel and useful.
sentences.zh: 最常见的定义可能是：要称得上具有创造力，就必须提出一个既新颖又有用的想法或产品。

sentences.en: I'm not crazy about that definition.
sentences.zh: 我不太喜欢这个定义。

sentences.en: It seems to be as close to a standard definition as we have at this point.
sentences.zh: 它似乎是我们目前所能达到的最接近标准定义的说法了。

sentences.en: So for something to be novel, obviously, has to be novel for the individual.
sentences.zh: 所以，要称得上“新颖”，显然必须对个人而言是新颖的。

sentences.en: So if I have never read Shakespeare's Hamlet, but I sit down and I write Hamlet, then it's novel to me.
sentences.zh: 如果我从未读过莎士比亚的《哈姆雷特》，但我坐下来写出了《哈姆雷特》，那么它对我来说就是新颖的。

sentences.en: It's not novel to the world, but at least it's novel to me.
sentences.zh: 它对世界来说并不新颖，但至少对我来说是新颖的。

sentences.en: It would be very creative if I could do that, not having read Shakespeare's Hamlet.
sentences.zh: 如果我能在没读过莎士比亚《哈姆雷特》的情况下做到这一点，那将是非常有创造力的。

sentences.en: Useful?
sentences.zh: “有用”呢？

sentences.en: That's a little bit harder.
sentences.zh: 这有点难界定。

sentences.en: Useful to whom?
sentences.zh: 对谁有用？

sentences.en: Certainly there are, for example, brilliant theorems that have been proven in mathematics that at the time were of no use to anyone.
sentences.zh: 当然，例如数学中证明了一些天才定理，但在当时对任何人都没有用处。

sentences.en: And perhaps 100 years later, theoretical physicists used it to come up with a novel understanding of, say, particle physics or string theory or whatever.
sentences.zh: 也许100年后，理论物理学家利用它对粒子物理学、弦理论或其他什么领域有了新的理解。

sentences.en: So something could be useful at one time and not be useful anymore later.
sentences.zh: 所以，某样东西可能在某个时期有用，后来就没用了。

sentences.en: So that's not a great definition either.
sentences.zh: 所以这也不是一个很好的定义。

sentences.en: Maybe a little bit better is to say that something is appropriate.
sentences.zh: 也许说某样东西是“恰当的”会更好一点。

sentences.en: So you could come up with an idea that is new to you, and it may not be right.
sentences.zh: 你可以想出一个对你来说是新的想法，但它可能是不正确的。

sentences.en: Perhaps it's a brilliant failure.
sentences.zh: 也许这是一个天才般的失败。

sentences.en: I mean, we all have had brilliant failures.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们都经历过天才般的失败。

sentences.en: They were creative, but they just didn't pan out.
sentences.zh: 它们是有创造力的，只是没有成功。

sentences.en: But at least they were appropriate to a particular problem or question or of some intereSt.
sentences.zh: 但至少它们对于特定的问题、疑问或某种兴趣点来说是恰当的。

sentences.en: So novel and useful, novel and appropriate.
sentences.zh: 所以是“新颖且有用”，或者“新颖且恰当”。

sentences.en: That's one way of thinking creativity.
sentences.zh: 这是思考创造力的一种方式。

sentences.en: Another approach, which I like a little better,
sentences.zh: 另一种我更喜欢的方法是，

sentences.en: is that creativity is the ability to take the elements of thought and break them down and reorganize them into something that is new.
sentences.zh: 创造力是拆解思维要素并将其重组为新事物的能力。

sentences.en: So, for example, you could take the notes of the musical scale and rearrange those to come up with a beautiful melody.
sentences.zh: 例如，你可以取音阶中的音符，重新排列它们，创作出一段美妙的旋律。

sentences.en: You could take words, rearrange those to come up with a poem.
sentences.zh: 你可以取词汇，重新排列它们，创作出一首诗。

sentences.en: You could take the elements of mathematical equations, rearrange those to come up with a new theorem, a new equation.
sentences.zh: 你可以取数学方程的要素，重新排列它们，得出一个新的定理或方程。

sentences.en: So I kind of like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我挺喜欢这种说法。

sentences.en: It gets away from the useful part.
sentences.zh: 它避开了“有用”这一部分。

sentences.en: I mean, it still has to have something appropriate to it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它仍然需要具备某种恰当性。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you have someone who has schizophrenia, they may be reorganizing all of their associations in novel ways.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果一个人患有精神分裂症，他们可能会以新颖的方式重组所有的联想。

sentences.en: But those could be kind of random.
sentences.zh: 但这些联想可能有点随机。

sentences.en: They're not really we wouldn't call it creative because it could be just gibberish.
sentences.zh: 我们不会称之为创造力，因为那可能只是胡言乱语。

sentences.en: If it has some purpose, some appropriateness, then we can still call that creativity.
sentences.zh: 如果它具有某种目的、某种恰当性，那么我们仍然可以称之为创造力。

sentences.en: Yet another possible way to think of creativity is the ability to think on your feet.
sentences.zh: 另一种思考创造力的方式是“随机应变”的能力。

sentences.en: So this is what what cognitive psychologists call fluid intelligence.
sentences.zh: 这就是认知心理学家所说的流体智力。

sentences.en: So it's your ability to deal with novel situations where you can't rely that much on past experience.
sentences.zh: 这是你在无法过多依赖过去经验的情况下处理新情况的能力。

sentences.en: You have to improvise.
sentences.zh: 你必须即兴发挥。

sentences.en: Think on your feet.
sentences.zh: 随机应变。

sentences.en: That would be one potential form of creativity.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一种潜在的创造力形式。

sentences.en: And as we can talk about later from our studies of musical improvisation,
sentences.zh: 正如我们稍后可以从我们的音乐即兴创作研究中谈到的那样，

sentences.en: it's creativity can be different for people who are novices in a particular field versus being experts in that field.
sentences.zh: 对于特定领域的新手和专家来说，创造力可能是不同的。

sentences.en: So those are just, you know, different ways of defining creativity.
sentences.zh: 所以这些只是定义创造力的不同方式。

sentences.en: And you can apply that to all areas of life, whether it's arts, the humanities, science, practical aspects of daily life, you know, trying to get a toddler to eat vegetables.
sentences.zh: 你可以将其应用于生活的各个领域，无论是艺术、人文、科学，还是日常生活的实际方面，比如试图让蹒跚学步的孩子吃蔬菜。

sentences.en: You might come up with some some great idea to do that.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想出一些很棒的点子来做到这一点。

sentences.en: Those are all forms of creativity.
sentences.zh: 这些都是创造力的形式。

sentences.en: So how do you study this?
sentences.zh: 那么你是如何研究这个问题的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, you use neuroimaging to look at what's happening in people's brains when they're having insights, but you can't necessarily predict when an insight will happen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你使用神经影像学来观察人们产生洞察时大脑中发生的情况，但你无法预测洞察何时会发生。

sentences.en: So how do you measure when someone is having an actual eureka moment?
sentences.zh: 那么你如何测量某人何时产生了真正的“尤里卡”时刻？

sentences.en: OK, so these eureka moments or aha moments, they're one form of creativity.
sentences.zh: 好的，这些“尤里卡”时刻或“啊哈”时刻是创造力的一种形式。

sentences.en: So one way to look at this is that since it's difficult to come up with a definition of creativity that everyone agrees on,
sentences.zh: 所以看待这个问题的一种方式是，由于很难得出一个大家都同意的创造力定义，

sentences.en: the approach that I've mostly taken in my research is to take some phenomena that everyone agrees is a manifestation of creativity.
sentences.zh: 我在研究中主要采取的方法是选取一些大家都公认是创造力表现的现象。

sentences.en: And these aha moments or eureka moments, researchers seem to have a consensus that those are one manifestation of creativity.
sentences.zh: 而这些“啊哈”时刻或“尤里卡”时刻，研究人员似乎达成了一种共识，即它们是创造力的一种表现。

sentences.en: So we can we can focus on that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以专注于此。

sentences.en: Now, the famous eureka moments, you know,
sentences.zh: 现在，那些著名的“尤里卡”时刻，你知道，

sentences.en: could be Isaac Newton with the apple falling in gravity or Paul McCartney having a dream and which gave him the melody for the song yesterday.
sentences.zh: 可能是艾萨克·牛顿看到苹果落地发现重力，或者是保罗·麦卡特尼做了一个梦，梦中给了他歌曲《昨日》的旋律。

sentences.en: All of these things, you know, these are kind of rare events.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情，你知道，都是些罕见的事件。

sentences.en: We can't chase people around, predict when they're going to have an aha moment or a cycle,
sentences.zh: 我们不能追着人跑，预测他们什么时候会有“啊哈”时刻，或者心理科学家称之为“洞察”的时刻，

sentences.en: psychological scientists call them an insight and then stuff them in a brain scanner and wait for it to happen.
sentences.zh: 然后把他们塞进脑部扫描仪里等着它发生。

sentences.en: We just can't do that.
sentences.zh: 我们做不到。

sentences.en: And a neuroimaging also requires not just a single instance of an aha moment.
sentences.zh: 而且神经影像学也不仅仅需要“啊哈”时刻的单一实例。

sentences.en: It requires multiple instances.
sentences.zh: 它需要多个实例。

sentences.en: We have to average over many of these things in order to extract the brain activity that's associated with your hama.
sentences.zh: 我们必须对许多这类事件进行平均，才能提取出与你的“啊哈”时刻相关的大脑活动。

sentences.en: So my colleague and collaborator, longstanding Mark Beeman, who's at Northwestern University, who also co-authored the book, The Eureka Factor, with me, many years ago,
sentences.zh: 所以我的长期同事和合作者，西北大学的马克·比曼，他也是《尤里卡因素》一书的合著者，多年前，

sentences.en: we decided to take a different approach.
sentences.zh: 我们决定采取一种不同的方法。

sentences.en: And that is instead of waiting for these insights to come, we would use little verbal puzzles that a person could solve in a few seconds and we could give people many of these.
sentences.zh: 那就是与其等待这些洞察出现，我们不如使用一些小型的语言谜题，一个人可以在几秒钟内解决，我们可以给人们提供很多这样的谜题。

sentences.en: So the analogy might be that biomedical researchers studying a disease, trying to come up with a cure for disease.
sentences.zh: 所以类比一下，研究疾病并试图寻找治愈方法的生物医学研究人员，

sentences.en: They use, say, a mouse model.
sentences.zh: 他们会使用，比如说，小鼠模型。

sentences.en: And the mouse model is, in many respects, I mean, mice are not humans, but they've been engineered genetically to have certain characteristics that would allow us to predict,
sentences.zh: 小鼠模型在许多方面——我的意思是，小鼠不是人类，但它们经过基因工程改造，具有某些特征，使我们能够预测，

sentences.en: based on how a mouse responds to things, whether this drug, for example, might be helpful for humans.
sentences.zh: 根据小鼠对事物的反应，这种药物是否可能对人类有帮助。

sentences.en: So we're sort of using a mouse model in a way.
sentences.zh: 所以我们也在某种程度上使用“小鼠模型”。

sentences.en: We use these little problems, which we have every reason to believe differ from the big Eureka moments only in their size or scope.
sentences.zh: 我们使用这些小问题，我们有充分的理由相信它们与大型“尤里卡”时刻的区别仅在于规模或范围。

sentences.en: We can give people many of these little puzzles and study the brain activity when people solve little puzzles that either with a flesh of insight or solve them analytically.
sentences.zh: 我们可以给人们提供许多这样的小谜题，并研究当人们通过灵光一现或分析性地解决这些小谜题时的大脑活动。

sentences.en: So we've selected types of puzzles, such as anagrams or other types called compound remote associates.
sentences.zh: 所以我们选择了特定类型的谜题，例如变位词或其他称为“复合远距离联想”的类型。

sentences.en: These are little puzzles that a person can solve in one of two ways.
sentences.zh: 这些是小谜题，一个人可以通过两种方式之一来解决。

sentences.en: They can solve it.
sentences.zh: 他们可以解决它。

sentences.en: Say you have an anagram.
sentences.zh: 假设你有一个变位词。

sentences.en: One way to solve the anagram is you consciously, deliberately, methodically rearrange the letters to find a word.
sentences.zh: 解决变位词的一种方法是你自觉、刻意、有条理地重新排列字母来找到一个单词。

sentences.en: We would call that analytical thinking.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为分析性思维。

sentences.en: That goes back.
sentences.zh: 这个术语可以追溯到100多年前。

sentences.en: That term goes back over 100 years.
sentences.zh: 你看着变位词，一两秒钟后，解决方案就突然跳入你的意识中。

sentences.en: You look at the anagram and then after a second or two, the solution just pops into your awareness.
sentences.zh: 它可能需要超过一两秒钟的时间。

sentences.en: It could take longer than a second or two.
sentences.zh: 你有了给你单词的“啊哈”时刻。

sentences.en: You have your aha moment that gives you the word.
sentences.zh: 那将是洞察或“啊哈”时刻。

sentences.en: That would be insight or an aha moment.
sentences.zh: 所以通过给人们提供大量这些谜题，并且对于他们解决的每一个谜题，我们都会问他们，

sentences.en: So by giving people lots of these puzzles and for each one that they solve, we ask them,
sentences.zh: 那是突然跳进你脑海的，还是通过某种自觉、刻意的方式推导出来的？

sentences.en: did that just pop into your head or did that result from sort of working it out in a conscious, deliberate way?
sentences.zh: 我们可以将解决方案分为“啊哈”时刻解决方案和分析性解决方案，并比较这两者的大脑活动。

sentences.en: We can sort the solutions into aha moment solutions and analytic solutions and compare the brain activity for the two of these.
sentences.zh: 我们可以观察当一个人通过突然的洞察解决问题与分析性解决问题时，大脑中哪些区域被独特地激活了。

sentences.en: And we can look at, you know, what are the brain areas that you are uniquely activated when a person solves the problem with a sudden insight versus solving it analytically.
sentences.zh: 所以你发现了证据表明有些人更倾向于分析性思维，而有些人更倾向于洞察性思维。

sentences.en: So you've found evidence that some people tend more toward analytical thinking and more toward insightful thinking.
sentences.zh: 但两者之间的实际区别是什么？

sentences.en: But what are the actual differences between the two?
sentences.zh: 大多数人是否更倾向于其中一种方向？

sentences.en: And do most people tend more strongly in one direction than the other?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, yes.
sentences.zh: 实际上，让我先退一步讲。

sentences.en: So actually, let me back up a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我们在2004年发表在《公共科学图书馆·生物学》上的初步研究中发现，对于特定类型的语言谜题，洞察本身，即“啊哈”时刻本身，

sentences.en: So what we found in our initial study, which we published in PLOS Biology in 2004, was that for a particular type of verbal puzzle, the insight itself, the aha moment itself,
sentences.zh: 对应于右颞叶（右耳上方）的一阵大脑活动。

sentences.en: corresponds to a burst of brain activity in the right temporal lobe, just above the right ear.
sentences.zh: 高频脑电图（EEG），以及使用功能性磁共振成像（fMRI），

sentences.en: High frequency EEG, and also electroencephalogram, and also using functional magnetic resonance imaging, fMRI,
sentences.zh: 在解决方案跳入意识的那一刻，血流量会增加。

sentences.en: an increase in blood flow just at the moment that the person has the solution pop into awareness.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们能够在一系列研究中追溯时间，找出导致一个人产生“啊哈”时刻的前兆是什么？

sentences.en: So we were able to then, over a series of studies, trace backwards in time, what are the precursors that lead to a person having an aha moment?
sentences.zh: 所以你在谈论人与人之间的个体差异，即有些人是否更有可能通过洞察力来解决这些谜题或任何类型的谜题，

sentences.en: And so you're talking about individual differences between people, which are some people more likely to solve these puzzles or any kind of puzzles by insight,
sentences.zh: 而另一些人更有可能通过分析来解决它们？

sentences.en: and others more likely to solve them analytically?
sentences.zh: 答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: And the answer is yes.
sentences.zh: 在我实验室由布莱恩·埃里克森领导的一项研究中，他现在是德雷塞尔大学的研究教授，这是他在我实验室博士论文研究的一部分。

sentences.en: So in a study led in my lab by Brian Erickson, who's now a research professor at Drexel University, this was part of his doctoral dissertation research in my lab.
sentences.zh: 这项研究由国家科学基金会资助，我们记录了人们的静息态脑电图，即他们的静息态EEG。

sentences.en: And the study was funded by the National Science Foundation, we recorded people's resting state electroencephalogram, they're resting state EEGs.
sentences.zh: 他们坐在那里，没有任务要执行，不知道接下来会发生什么，只是坐着放松，我们记录他们的大脑活动。

sentences.en: So they're sitting there, no task to perform, no idea what's going to come next, they're just sitting and relaxing, we record their brain activity.
sentences.zh: 几周后，我们给他们提供变位词来解决。

sentences.en: And then weeks later, we give them, in this case, anagrams to solve.
sentences.zh: 我们记录每个受试者，你知道，哪些是他们分析性解决的，哪些是他们通过“啊哈”时刻洞察性解决的。

sentences.en: And we note for each subject, you know, which ones they solved analytically, and which ones they solved insightfully, within a aha moment.
sentences.zh: 然后我们将受试者分组，哪些人倾向于通过灵光一现解决问题，哪些人倾向于更多地通过分析解决问题。

sentences.en: We then divided the subjects into groups, which ones tended to solve the problems with a flash of insight, and which ones tended to solve more problems analytically.
sentences.zh: 我们比较了我们几周前记录的静息态大脑活动，发现这两类人之间存在显著差异。

sentences.en: And we compared the resting state brain activity that we recorded weeks earlier, and we found substantial differences between these two types of people.
sentences.zh: 首先，令人惊奇的是，静息态大脑活动的记录可以在几周前预测你的认知风格是洞察型还是分析型，

sentences.en: So first of all, it's amazing that recordings of resting state brain activity can predict your cognitive style in cycle versus analytic, weeks in advance,
sentences.zh: 至少提前七周，甚至可能更久。

sentences.en: up to seven weeks in advance, at least, maybe longer.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有确定这一点。

sentences.en: We haven't, we haven't, we haven't determined that yet.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的是，分析型思考者在静息状态下，额叶的大脑活动往往更多。

sentences.en: And what we found is that the analytical thinkers, in their resting state, tend to have more brain activity over the frontal lobe, we could record over the frontal lobes.
sentences.zh: 而洞察型思考者在大脑左后部往往有更多的静息态大脑活动。

sentences.en: And the insightful thinkers tend to have more resting state brain activity in left posterior parts of the brain.
sentences.zh: 额叶是我们所谓的执行处理、认知控制的所在地。

sentences.en: So the frontal lobe is the seat of what we call executive processing, cognitive control.
sentences.zh: 它赋予我们专注力，设定目标，集中注意力。

sentences.en: It gives us focus, it sets goals, it focuses attention.
sentences.zh: 当额叶去激活时，即不那么活跃时，思维就会变得模糊、目标导向性降低、组织性降低。

sentences.en: When the frontal lobe is more deactivated, it's less active, then thinking becomes sort of fuzzier, less goal-directed, less organized.
sentences.zh: 而额叶活动较少的人，至少平均而言，往往会有更多的“啊哈”时刻，即突然的洞察。

sentences.en: And people who have less frontal lobe activity, at least on average, tend to have more of these aha moments, these sudden insights.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们往往在洗澡时，比如洗个舒服的热水澡时，会有这些“啊哈”时刻的原因。

sentences.en: And that's sort of why people tend to have these aha moments when they're, say, in the shower, you know, taking a nice warm shower.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们往往在洗澡时，比如洗个舒服的热水澡时，会有这些“啊哈”时刻的原因。

sentences.en: They're relaxed, it feels good, they don't have anything else to do at the moment, their minds wander, you know.
sentences.zh: 他们处于放松状态，感觉很好，当下没什么别的事要做，思绪就会飘忽不定，你知道的。

sentences.en: And they get relaxed, and in that fuzzy state, then they can have aha moments.
sentences.zh: 当他们放松下来，进入那种模糊的状态时，就可能会有“啊哈”时刻。

sentences.en: But if, you know, you have a couple of cups of coffee, you have a test to perform, you maybe have a deadline, you're very focused, that boosts analytical thinking.
sentences.zh: 但如果你喝了几杯咖啡，还要完成一项测试，或者面临截止日期，你就会非常专注，这会促进分析性思维。

sentences.en: And you tend to work things out in a more methodical, deliberate way.
sentences.zh: 你会倾向于用更系统、更深思熟虑的方式来解决问题。

sentences.en: So, yes, so there are analytical thinkers, there are insightful thinkers, on average.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，平均而言，既有分析型思考者，也有洞察型思考者。

sentences.en: I mean, virtually all of the subjects we've tested, and we've tested hundreds of subjects over the years,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们测试过的几乎所有受试者，多年来我们测试了数百名受试者，

sentences.en: virtually all of them solve some puzzles with insight and some puzzles analytically.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎所有人都是通过洞察力解决一些难题，通过分析解决另一些难题。

sentences.en: There's no one who's, you know, never has an aha moment that we've found, and no one who never thinks analytically.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，没有人是从来没有过“啊哈”时刻的，也没有人是从来不进行分析性思考的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just that some people tend to be balanced more one way or the other.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，只是有些人倾向于在某一方面更平衡一些。

sentences.en: And you can sort of nudge people one way or the other in various ways, and we can talk about that, too.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过各种方式引导人们偏向某一方，我们也可以谈谈这个。

sentences.en: But that really resonates.
sentences.zh: 但这确实引起了共鸣。

sentences.en: I'm a great fan of the New York Times spelling bee, right, which is you get seven words every morning, and you have to arrange them into words.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》拼字游戏的忠实粉丝，就是那种每天早上给你七个字母，你必须把它们组合成单词的游戏。

sentences.en: And I see myself, sometimes I'm thinking analytically to come up with them, and other times I just look at all the letters, and boom, there's a word.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己有时会通过分析来想出单词，而有时我只是看着所有的字母，砰的一声，单词就出来了。

sentences.en: So I get exactly what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以我完全明白你在说什么。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the different hemispheres of the brain.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈大脑的不同半球吧。

sentences.en: There's kind of an accepted wisdom that one side of the brain is where we do our creative thinking, the right side, yeah?
sentences.zh: 有一种公认的说法是，大脑的一侧是我们进行创造性思维的地方，也就是右脑，对吧？

sentences.en: And that the left side controls our analytical abilities, such as speech, mathematics, things like that.
sentences.zh: 而左脑控制我们的分析能力，比如语言、数学之类的东西。

sentences.en: And in some sense, we're told that never the twain meet.
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，我们被告知这两者永远不会交汇。

sentences.en: Now, you've done some research with jazz musicians that has pretty much turned that thinking on its head, to make a bad pun.
sentences.zh: 现在，你对爵士乐手进行了一些研究，这几乎颠覆了那种想法，这算是一个蹩脚的双关语。

sentences.en: What did you learn from that research about creativity and the two hemispheres of the brain?
sentences.zh: 你从那项关于创造力和大脑两个半球的研究中学到了什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so the study that you're talking about was published last year in NeuroImage, also funded by the National Science Foundation.
sentences.zh: 好的，你提到的那项研究去年发表在《NeuroImage》杂志上，也得到了美国国家科学基金会的资助。

sentences.en: And it was led by David Rosen, who at the time was a graduate student in my lab.
sentences.zh: 它由大卫·罗森（David Rosen）领导，他当时是我实验室的研究生。

sentences.en: And so the topic of the hemispheres of the brain and creativity is a very controversial topic among psychologists and neuroscientists.
sentences.zh: 大脑半球与创造力的话题在心理学家和神经科学家中是一个非常有争议的话题。

sentences.en: So, you know, the pop wisdom going back, oh, at least to the 1960s, is that, you know, the right hemisphere of the brain is creative.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，从20世纪60年代起流传的流行智慧是，大脑的右半球是创造性的。

sentences.en: The left hemisphere is logical and analytical.
sentences.zh: 左半球是逻辑和分析性的。

sentences.en: And that is a leap from early studies that were done on patients who had the hemispheres of their brains separated to help inhibit epileptic seizures.
sentences.zh: 这源于早期对那些为了抑制癫痫发作而切断大脑半球连接的患者所做的研究。

sentences.en: Right, so surgically separated, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是通过手术分离，对吧。

sentences.en: Surgically separated, right.
sentences.zh: 通过手术分离，没错。

sentences.en: And it was quite a leap.
sentences.zh: 那确实是一个很大的飞跃。

sentences.en: But the idea infused the pop culture.
sentences.zh: 但这个想法渗透到了流行文化中。

sentences.en: And we talk about right brain thinkers and left brain thinkers.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论右脑型思考者和左脑型思考者。

sentences.en: So neuroscientists correctly say that, you know, the normal brain is not cut in half, okay?
sentences.zh: 所以神经科学家正确地指出，正常的大脑并没有被切成两半，好吗？

sentences.en: The two hemispheres of the brain work together.
sentences.zh: 大脑的两个半球是一起工作的。

sentences.en: They work together almost all the time, okay?
sentences.zh: 它们几乎一直都在一起工作，好吗？

sentences.en: So it can't be that the right hemisphere is the creative hemisphere and the left hemisphere is the analytical hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 所以不可能是右半球是创造性半球，左半球是分析性半球。

sentences.en: It can't be.
sentences.zh: 这不可能。

sentences.en: The whole brain's involved.
sentences.zh: 整个大脑都参与其中。

sentences.en: Well, that's going a bit far, too.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那也有点言过其实了。

sentences.en: Because what the research has shown, in our case with our study of particular types of these puzzles, is that the aha moment, the brain activity, at the moment of insight,
sentences.zh: 因为研究表明，就我们对这些特定类型谜题的研究而言，那个“啊哈”时刻，即洞察力产生的那一刻的脑部活动，

sentences.en: is a burst of activity in the right temporal lobe.
sentences.zh: 是右颞叶的一阵活动。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's the right hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，那是右半球。

sentences.en: It's kind of suggestive right there.
sentences.zh: 这就在那里暗示了什么。

sentences.en: There's something going on.
sentences.zh: 确实有些事情正在发生。

sentences.en: Work that my colleague Mark Beeman and his longtime collaborator Ed Bowden have done, behavioral work mostly,
sentences.zh: 我的同事马克·比曼（Mark Beeman）和他长期的合作者埃德·鲍登（Ed Bowden）所做的工作，主要是行为学研究，

sentences.en: and also research that presents information directly to one hemisphere of the brain or the other,
sentences.zh: 以及直接向大脑一侧或另一侧呈现信息的研究，

sentences.en: suggests that the right hemisphere of the brain processes what we call remote associations.
sentences.zh: 表明大脑右半球处理我们所说的远距离联想。

sentences.en: So, for example, if I say the word water, you might think of the word glass, okay?
sentences.zh: 例如，如果我说“水”这个词，你可能会想到“玻璃”这个词，对吧？

sentences.en: That's a word that comes to mind immediately because those are close associations.
sentences.zh: 这是一个立刻浮现在脑海中的词，因为它们是紧密联想。

sentences.en: You think of a glass of water.
sentences.zh: 你会想到一杯水。

sentences.en: If I were to say the word water and then you came up with the word table, right, like water table, okay, that is a remote association.
sentences.zh: 如果我说“水”，然后你想到“桌子”，对吧，比如“水桌”，那是一个远距离联想。

sentences.en: It's not the first thing that comes to most people's minds.
sentences.zh: 这不是大多数人脑海中首先想到的东西。

sentences.en: Bowden and Beeman's research suggests that these remote associations tend to be stored in the right hemisphere of the brain and that the left hemisphere of the brain processes close associations.
sentences.zh: 鲍登和比曼的研究表明，这些远距离联想倾向于存储在大脑右半球，而大脑左半球处理紧密联想。

sentences.en: So, if I say water and you say glass, that's left hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我说“水”，你说“玻璃”，那是左半球。

sentences.en: If I say water and you say table, that's right hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 如果我说“水”，你说“桌子”，那是右半球。

sentences.en: And the right hemisphere is necessary for, for example, understanding the gist, understanding humor, understanding things that are not like face value, straightforward, okay?
sentences.zh: 右半球对于理解要点、理解幽默、理解那些不是字面意思、不直白的东西是必要的，好吗？

sentences.en: And that work still holds up and there's something to it.
sentences.zh: 这项工作仍然站得住脚，而且确实有其道理。

sentences.en: But we can take that a step further.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以更进一步。

sentences.en: So, there's, what we found in our study of jazz improvisation, we measured people's EEGs while they improvised on the guitar, jazz.
sentences.zh: 我们在爵士即兴演奏的研究中发现，我们在人们用吉他进行爵士即兴演奏时测量了他们的脑电图。

sentences.en: And some of these musicians were experts who had been performing jazz gigs for decades and decades.
sentences.zh: 其中一些音乐家是几十年来一直进行爵士乐演出的专家。

sentences.en: They were really good at it.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很擅长。

sentences.en: Others were novices and hadn't been doing it very long.
sentences.zh: 其他人是新手，练习时间不长。

sentences.en: And then we had people who were in between.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人处于中间水平。

sentences.en: So, we looked at, for each subject, we looked at their, they did a series of improvisations.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们观察了每个受试者，他们进行了一系列即兴演奏。

sentences.en: And we had experts later on rate the creativity of each improvisation, not knowing who actually performed.
sentences.zh: 我们让专家在不知道表演者是谁的情况下，对每次即兴演奏的创造力进行评分。

sentences.en: So, we looked at the best versus the worst improvisations for each subject, okay, in terms of most creative versus least creative.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们观察了每个受试者最好和最差的即兴演奏，也就是最具创造力和最不具创造力的。

sentences.en: And what we found is that experts' improvisation, their best versus their worst, activated the left posterior parts of the brain.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，专家的即兴演奏，即他们最好与最差的对比，激活了大脑的左后部区域。

sentences.en: For the novices, their best versus their worst activated the right hemisphere, mostly right frontal areas of the brain.
sentences.zh: 对于新手来说，他们最好与最差的对比激活了右半球，主要是大脑的右额叶区域。

sentences.en: But, we found this surprising.
sentences.zh: 但是，我们觉得这很令人惊讶。

sentences.en: So, looking around in the literature, there's kind of an old theory of the hemispheres in creativity that was first proposed by a neuropsychologist named Elkonen Goldberg.
sentences.zh: 查阅文献后，有一种关于创造力中半球作用的古老理论，最初是由一位名叫埃尔科农·戈德堡（Elkonen Goldberg）的神经心理学家提出的。

sentences.en: And what he argued is that the right hemisphere processes novel, stimuli, novel experiences.
sentences.zh: 他认为右半球处理新颖的刺激、新颖的体验。

sentences.en: When there's something new for you, a new task, a new stimulus, it's the right hemisphere that's engaged.
sentences.zh: 当你遇到新事物、新任务、新刺激时，是右半球在参与。

sentences.en: As you become more and more practiced at it, as it becomes more and more familiar, that activity moves to the left hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 随着你练习得越来越多，随着它变得越来越熟悉，这种活动就会转移到左半球。

sentences.en: So, for example, in most people, the left hemisphere is dominant for language because adults are so practiced at language.
sentences.zh: 例如，在大多数人中，左半球在语言方面占主导地位，因为成年人对语言非常熟练。

sentences.en: It moves from the left to the right.
sentences.zh: 它从左向右移动。

sentences.en: So, what this looks like, in our case with our jazz musicians, is that for the novices, improvisation is still not that familiar for them.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们的爵士乐手案例中，对于新手来说，即兴演奏对他们来说还不是很熟悉。

sentences.en: It's still kind of a new experience.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是一种新的体验。

sentences.en: And when they have to improvise, they improvise in our study to set chord and rhythm sequences that we gave them.
sentences.zh: 当他们必须即兴演奏时，他们在我们的研究中是根据我们给出的和弦和节奏序列进行即兴演奏的。

sentences.en: This was sort of an unfamiliar task.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不熟悉的任务。

sentences.en: So, they work it out, you know, deliberately, analytically, if you will.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们会刻意地、分析性地解决它，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: They're consciously strategizing.
sentences.zh: 他们是有意识地制定策略。

sentences.en: All right, I'll do this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我这样做。

sentences.en: Now, we'll do that.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们那样做。

sentences.en: That didn't sound so good.
sentences.zh: 那听起来不太好。

sentences.en: Now, we'll try this.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们试试这个。

sentences.en: That worked better.
sentences.zh: 那个效果更好。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The experts don't do that.
sentences.zh: 专家们不会那样做。

sentences.en: The experts, if they've been doing this long enough, and they really have been, many of them did it for decades and decades, they just sort of turn it on, like a faucet,
sentences.zh: 专家们，如果他们做这件事足够久，而且他们确实做得很久，许多人做了几十年，他们只是像打开水龙头一样打开它，

sentences.en: and it just flows.
sentences.zh: 它就自然流淌出来了。

sentences.en: It just flows.
sentences.zh: 它就自然流淌出来了。

sentences.en: And so, the novices are using more of this think-on-your-feet type of creativity.
sentences.zh: 所以，新手使用的是更多这种“临场发挥”式的创造力。

sentences.en: But as the years of practice go by, it shifts to the left hemisphere, and it becomes more, just turn it on, it's automatic, it flows.
sentences.zh: 但随着练习年份的增加，它会转移到左半球，变得更加自动化，只要打开开关，它就会自然流淌。

sentences.en: You don't have to think about it.
sentences.zh: 你不需要去思考它。

sentences.en: And that may relate to this idea, this older idea, it's not that old, of Beeman and Bowden, and that I've worked on also, of remote association.
sentences.zh: 这可能与比曼和鲍登提出的那个想法有关，那个想法并不算太旧，我也参与过研究，即远距离联想。

sentences.en: So, in the right hemisphere, so when you get something that's new, it's remote, it's a remote association.
sentences.zh: 所以，在右半球，当你得到一些新的东西时，它是遥远的，是一个远距离联想。

sentences.en: You don't think of that normally.
sentences.zh: 你通常不会想到那个。

sentences.en: So, if I were to say, water table, water table, it might be a new idea for you.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我说“水桌”，那对你来说可能是一个新想法。

sentences.en: But if you start thinking and reading about water tables a lot, it might move from the right hemisphere to the left hemisphere, eventually, because it becomes practiced.
sentences.zh: 但如果你开始思考并阅读大量关于水桌的内容，它最终可能会从右半球转移到左半球，因为它变得熟练了。

sentences.en: So, this might be a way of thinking about the hemispheres and creativity.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可能是思考半球和创造力的一种方式。

sentences.en: It may be that it's not sort of creative in the right hemisphere versus uncreative in the left hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 可能并不是右半球有创造力而左半球没有创造力。

sentences.en: What it may be, and what the newest data suggests, is that the right hemisphere, and especially the right frontal lobe,
sentences.zh: 情况可能是，最新的数据表明，右半球，尤其是右额叶，

sentences.en: is especially good at and very important for creativity in terms of thinking on your feet, dealing with a novel situation, something that's unfamiliar.
sentences.zh: 在临场发挥、处理新情况、不熟悉的事物方面的创造力方面特别擅长且非常重要。

sentences.en: It might be what intelligence researchers call fluid intelligence, whereas the left hemisphere is more of the focus on this practiced creativity.
sentences.zh: 这可能是智力研究人员所说的流体智力，而左半球更多地关注这种熟练的创造力。

sentences.en: It would practice in that particular genre or test, say musical improvisation, could be other things.
sentences.zh: 它会在特定的流派或测试中进行练习，比如音乐即兴演奏，也可以是其他事情。

sentences.en: It gets baked in.
sentences.zh: 它被固化了。

sentences.en: It becomes more effortless.
sentences.zh: 它变得更加不费力。

sentences.en: You don't, a lot of it becomes unconscious.
sentences.zh: 你不需要，很多东西变得无意识了。

sentences.en: The music just flows and goes right to your hands as you're performing.
sentences.zh: 音乐只是流淌出来，并在你表演时直接传到你的手上。

sentences.en: So, that is sort of our latest way of thinking about creativity in the brain.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我们关于大脑创造力的最新思考方式。

sentences.en: And so, in a sense, the right hemisphere, according to this idea, is the seat of one form of creativity, and that is this ability to deal with novelty.
sentences.zh: 因此，在某种意义上，根据这个观点，右半球是某种形式创造力的所在地，那就是处理新奇事物的能力。

sentences.en: Whereas the left hemisphere is this ability to take from baked in experience, longstanding experience, and process the information unconsciously, and then it just flows.
sentences.zh: 而左半球则是从固化的经验、长期的经验中汲取信息，并无意识地处理这些信息，然后它就自然流淌出来了。

sentences.en: That kind of speaks to the idea of creative geniuses in human history, like you mentioned Isaac Newton and the falling apple, you know, Thomas Edison and the electric light,
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上印证了人类历史上创造性天才的想法，比如你提到的艾萨克·牛顿和掉落的苹果，你知道，托马斯·爱迪生和电灯，

sentences.en: for example.
sentences.zh: 例如。

sentences.en: And there's some thinking that these insights arise spontaneously, and yet if you look more closely at the lives of some of these people,
sentences.zh: 有人认为这些洞察力是自发产生的，但如果你仔细观察其中一些人的生活，

sentences.en: they've actually spent hundreds of hours working at their craft or their science before they reach these achievements.
sentences.zh: 他们在取得这些成就之前，实际上已经花费了数百小时在他们的技艺或科学上。

sentences.en: I'm just wondering, how much of genius, as we call it, consists of aha moments, and how much is only possible because of the obsessive focus on a particular specialty,
sentences.zh: 我只是想知道，我们所说的天才，有多少是由“啊哈”时刻组成的，又有多少仅仅是因为对特定专业的痴迷才成为可能的，

sentences.en: whether it's music or science or painting, whatever it is that you're obsessed with?
sentences.zh: 无论是音乐、科学还是绘画，无论你痴迷于什么？

sentences.en: It depends on what you want to be creative about.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你想在什么方面有创造力。

sentences.en: So, everyone is an expert at something.
sentences.zh: 所以，每个人都是某方面的专家。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone is an expert at daily life.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每个人都是日常生活中的专家。

sentences.en: Nobody knows your daily life better than you do.
sentences.zh: 没有人比你更了解你的日常生活。

sentences.en: So, since you're an expert at daily life, you're in a position to have these aha moments about how to do things in your daily life.
sentences.zh: 所以，既然你是日常生活中的专家，你就有能力在如何处理日常生活琐事上拥有这些“啊哈”时刻。

sentences.en: Not everyone is in a position to have aha moments about particle physics.
sentences.zh: 并不是每个人都有能力在粒子物理学上拥有“啊哈”时刻。

sentences.en: I mean, that takes years of study.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那需要多年的学习。

sentences.en: It takes a lot of analytical ability to understand the mathematics and the experimentation involved.
sentences.zh: 理解其中涉及的数学和实验需要大量的分析能力。

sentences.en: So, if you want to be creative about particle physics, you've got to do your homework, years and years of homework, and then you'll be in a position to have these amazing insights.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想在粒子物理学方面有创造力，你必须做功课，多年的功课，然后你才有能力拥有这些惊人的洞察力。

sentences.en: You need the immersion and the practice to gain the specialized knowledge.
sentences.zh: 你需要沉浸和练习来获得专业知识。

sentences.en: But you don't necessarily need to have immersion in a particular question or problem.
sentences.zh: 但你不一定需要沉浸在特定的问题或难题中。

sentences.en: So, for example, it's well known, the idea that you have a question or a problem, and you might have an aha moment later on,
sentences.zh: 例如，众所周知，你有一个问题或难题，你可能会在稍后有一个“啊哈”时刻，

sentences.en: whether you're in the shower or it wakes you up during the night or something like that.
sentences.zh: 无论是在洗澡时，还是在夜里醒来时，或者类似的情况。

sentences.en: But there are instances where people have an aha moment that gives them a solution or an idea.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些例子，人们拥有一个“啊哈”时刻，给他们一个解决方案或想法。

sentences.en: It's like a solution to a problem they didn't even know they had.
sentences.zh: 就像是一个他们甚至不知道自己有的问题的解决方案。

sentences.en: So, one example that I really love of this is that there was this engineer aboard a Navy ship, U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，我非常喜欢的一个例子是，1943年，一艘海军舰艇上有一位工程师，美国海军舰艇。

sentences.en: Navy ship, in 1943.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫理查德·詹姆斯（Richard James），他的工作是安装弹簧，就像减震器一样，

sentences.en: His name was Richard James, and his job was to install springs to, like shock absorbers,
sentences.zh: 用来缓冲仪器，这样当海面波涛汹涌，船只被颠簸时，仪器就会保持稳定，比如仪表之类的东西。

sentences.en: to cushion instruments so that when there was a rough sea and the ship was being buffeted about, the instruments would be stabilized, like gauges and things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，他正在安装弹簧，然后其中一个弹簧松脱了，开始像有生命一样跳来跳去。

sentences.en: So, he's installing the springs, and then one of the springs got loose and started bouncing around like it had a life of its own.
sentences.zh: 所以，他看着那个，心想，哇，这会是一个很棒的玩具。

sentences.en: So, he looked at that, he thought, wow, this would make a great toy.
sentences.zh: 经过一番开发，它就成了弹簧玩具（Slinky）。

sentences.en: And after some development, it became the slinky.
sentences.zh: 现在，他在那之前在想玩具吗？

sentences.en: Now, was he thinking about toys before that?
sentences.zh: 我怀疑。

sentences.en: I doubt it.
sentences.zh: 没有证据表明这一点。

sentences.en: There's no evidence of that.
sentences.zh: 只是，他看到了这个，它在他脑海中激发了这个想法，并不是说他一直在酝酿或纠结这个问题很长时间。

sentences.en: It just, he saw this, it sparked this idea in his head, and it wasn't as if he had been sort of incubating or struggling with this problem for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个伟大的想法，是一个他不知道自己有的问题的解决方案。

sentences.en: It was just a great idea that was a solution to a problem he didn't know he had.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，再次强调，洞察力、创造力可以是自发的。

sentences.en: And so, you know, again, so insight, creativity, can be spontaneous.
sentences.zh: 它不一定非要由问题触发。

sentences.en: It doesn't have to be triggered by a problem.
sentences.zh: 它可能只是发生了。

sentences.en: It could just happen.
sentences.zh: 这就是创造力令人惊奇的地方之一，它的自发性，以及它偶尔是某种产物，你知道，

sentences.en: And that's one of the amazing things about creativity is that it, the spontaneity of it, as well as it being the product occasionally of, you know,
sentences.zh: 对问题或目标的刻意钻研。

sentences.en: deliberate grappling with a problem or a goal.
sentences.zh: 那么，人们可以做些什么来鼓励这种创造性的洞察力呢？

sentences.en: So, what can people do to encourage this kind of creative insight?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们可以做些什么来鼓励这种创造性的洞察力呢？

sentences.en: I mean, are there things that we can do that will spark more aha moments in our lives?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们能做些什么来激发生活中更多的灵光一现时刻吗？

sentences.en: Because I think we'd all like to be more creative.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得我们都希望能更有创造力。

sentences.en: So, there are, and this is ongoing research that will be, I mean, some of it's well-established, some is emerging, others will, other aspects of it will, in a number of years,
sentences.zh: 所以，确实有办法，而且这是一项正在进行的研究，有些部分已经很成熟，有些还在萌芽阶段，还有其他方面，在未来几年内，

sentences.en: we'll know for sure.
sentences.zh: 我们就能确定了。

sentences.en: But let's start with sort of the basics of what we know.
sentences.zh: 但让我们先从我们已知的基础知识开始吧。

sentences.en: So, there is a principle in psychological safety.
sentences.zh: 首先，心理安全感中存在一个原则。

sentences.en: You can feel safe and unthreatened, or you can feel threatened and anxious.
sentences.zh: 你可以感到安全且不受威胁，也可以感到受威胁且焦虑。

sentences.en: So, for example, when, say you're an early human on the savannah in Africa, and you see a lion way off in the distance, at that moment,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，假设你是非洲大草原上的早期人类，你远远地看到了一头狮子，在那一刻，

sentences.en: you're going to become very focused and anxious.
sentences.zh: 你会变得非常专注且焦虑。

sentences.en: Because if that lion detects you, you're finished, right?
sentences.zh: 因为如果那头狮子发现了你，你就完了，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you're going to freeze, you're going to focus on the lion, you're going to think, all right, has the lion detected me?
sentences.zh: 所以，你会僵住，你会盯着狮子看，你会想，好吧，狮子发现我了吗？

sentences.en: What can I do to avoid being detected?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么做才能避免被发现？

sentences.en: Am I upwind or downwind of the lion?
sentences.zh: 我在狮子的上风向还是下风向？

sentences.en: Am I going to make noise?
sentences.zh: 我会发出声音吗？

sentences.en: If I run away, will the lion see the motion?
sentences.zh: 如果我逃跑，狮子会看到动作吗？

sentences.en: You're going to be really careful.
sentences.zh: 你会变得非常谨慎。

sentences.en: That is analytical thinking.
sentences.zh: 这就是分析性思维。

sentences.en: It's deliberate, it's focused, it's very organized, because you can't afford to make a mistake.
sentences.zh: 它是深思熟虑的、专注的、非常有条理的，因为你承担不起犯错的代价。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you're still that early human.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你依然是那个早期人类。

sentences.en: You're in your cave at night with your clan.
sentences.zh: 晚上你和你的族群待在洞穴里。

sentences.en: You're all well-fed.
sentences.zh: 你们都吃饱了。

sentences.en: You're all safe.
sentences.zh: 你们都很安全。

sentences.en: You feel relaxed.
sentences.zh: 你感到放松。

sentences.en: When you're relaxed, there's no threat.
sentences.zh: 当你放松时，就没有威胁。

sentences.en: When there's no threat, your attention expands.
sentences.zh: 当没有威胁时，你的注意力就会扩展。

sentences.en: You can, there's no risk.
sentences.zh: 你可以，没有任何风险。

sentences.en: There's no risk to thinking crazy thoughts.
sentences.zh: 想些疯狂的念头没有任何风险。

sentences.en: There's no risk to exploring, you know, off-the-wall ideas.
sentences.zh: 去探索那些天马行空的想法也没有任何风险。

sentences.en: And it's very different from the lion situation, because in the lion situation, you can't make a mistake.
sentences.zh: 这和面对狮子的情况截然不同，因为在面对狮子时，你不能犯错。

sentences.en: You have to be really careful.
sentences.zh: 你必须非常小心。

sentences.en: You can't try things out, right?
sentences.zh: 你不能尝试各种可能，对吧？

sentences.en: So, what we know from long-standing research by many researchers is that creativity is enhanced by a positive mood.
sentences.zh: 所以，从许多研究人员长期以来的研究中我们得知，积极的情绪能增强创造力。

sentences.en: When you're in a positive mood, you have this feeling of psychological safety.
sentences.zh: 当你处于积极的情绪中时，你会有一种心理安全感。

sentences.en: Your attention expands.
sentences.zh: 你的注意力会扩展。

sentences.en: You become less self-critical.
sentences.zh: 你对自己的批评会减少。

sentences.en: But when you're anxious, and that anxiety could be caused by a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 但当你感到焦虑时，而这种焦虑可能由很多原因引起。

sentences.en: It could be fear of embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 它可能是对出丑的恐惧。

sentences.en: It could be a deadline.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个截止日期。

sentences.en: It could be a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 这可能是很多原因。

sentences.en: You become more analytical.
sentences.zh: 你会变得更具分析性。

sentences.en: You do things in a very careful way.
sentences.zh: 你会以非常谨慎的方式做事。

sentences.en: And, you know, analytical thinking can still result in a creative product.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，分析性思维依然可以产生创造性的成果。

sentences.en: So, for example, if I give you a task to come up with a number of ideas and say they all have to be creative, you'll probably, and you have, like, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果我给你一个任务，让你想出一些点子，并要求它们都必须具有创造性，你可能会——而且你确实有——你知道，

sentences.en: 10 minutes to do it,
sentences.zh: 十分钟的时间来完成，

sentences.en: you'll probably, that deadline will make you focus and be very analytical.
sentences.zh: 你可能会，那个截止日期会让你集中注意力并变得非常具有分析性。

sentences.en: But you'll probably consciously reject all of the non-creative ideas.
sentences.zh: 但你很可能会有意识地拒绝所有非创造性的点子。

sentences.en: So, what you present will be the best, the most creative of your thinking, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，你呈现出来的将是你思维中最棒、最有创造力的部分，对吧？

sentences.en: You filter.
sentences.zh: 你在进行筛选。

sentences.en: You use your analytical focus thinking to filter yourself out.
sentences.zh: 你利用你的分析性专注思维来过滤掉不好的想法。

sentences.en: So, but in general, positive mood enhances insightful thinking, anxiety, and anything that causes focus will result in more analytical thinking.
sentences.zh: 所以，总的来说，积极的情绪能增强洞察性思维，而焦虑以及任何导致专注的事物都会带来更多的分析性思维。

sentences.en: And this also, you can extend this to this idea of expanding attention.
sentences.zh: 这一点也可以延伸到扩展注意力的概念上。

sentences.en: So, for example, if a person is in an expansive environment, they go outside, or they're in a big room with high ceilings,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果一个人处于一个广阔的环境中，他们走到户外，或者待在一个天花板很高的宽敞房间里，

sentences.en: there's a link between what's called perceptual attention and conceptual attention.
sentences.zh: 所谓的感知注意力与概念注意力之间存在着一种联系。

sentences.en: The two are linked.
sentences.zh: 这两者是相互关联的。

sentences.en: When your attention expands to fill a large space, that expansion of perceptual attention also expands conceptual attention.
sentences.zh: 当你的注意力扩展到填满一个大空间时，这种感知注意力的扩展也会带动概念注意力的扩展。

sentences.en: So, that's why a lot of creative figures, they like to take walks in nature or even in the shower.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是为什么许多创意人士喜欢在自然中散步，甚至喜欢在淋浴时思考的原因。

sentences.en: You know, there's white noise, your vision is kind of blurred, you can't sense the, it's a hot shower,
sentences.zh: 你知道，会有白噪音，视线变得模糊，你无法感知到……就像洗热水澡一样，

sentences.en: you can't sense the boundary between what's outside of your skin and what's inside.
sentences.zh: 你无法感知到皮肤内外之间的界限。

sentences.en: You kind of feel almost disembodied.
sentences.zh: 你会感觉自己几乎脱离了躯体。

sentences.en: And that allows your attention to expand.
sentences.zh: 这能让你的注意力得到扩展。

sentences.en: And you can get these crazy, wonderful ideas.
sentences.zh: 然后你就能产生那些疯狂而美妙的想法。

sentences.en: But if you're in a cubicle, and you're guzzling coffee, and you've got something due in an hour, your attention will narrow and focus and become analytic.
sentences.zh: 但如果你坐在隔间里，狂喝咖啡，还要在一小时内赶工，你的注意力就会收窄、聚焦，变得分析性极强。

sentences.en: So, you can sort of jumpstart this expansion of attention by being in wide open spaces and avoiding things that grab your attention.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以通过置身于广阔的开放空间，并避开那些会吸引你注意力的事物，来启动这种注意力的扩展。

sentences.en: It could be striking works of art.
sentences.zh: 这可能是引人注目的艺术作品。

sentences.en: It could be anything that grabs your attention, bright colors, that will narrow your focus.
sentences.zh: 任何吸引你注意力的东西，比如鲜艳的色彩，都会让你的焦点收窄。

sentences.en: So, being in sort of, you know, fuzzy, warm environments, kind of new agey, all of that, attention expands, and it expands the scope of thought.
sentences.zh: 所以，身处那种模糊、温暖的环境，或者类似新纪元风格的地方，注意力就会扩展，思维的广度也会随之增加。

sentences.en: Another thing is working, doing your creative work, when your thinking is a little fuzzy.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，在思维有点模糊的时候进行创造性工作。

sentences.en: So, some people are morning people, some people are evening people.
sentences.zh: 有些人是晨型人，有些人是夜型人。

sentences.en: Well, you do your best analytical thinking at your peak time, whether it's morning or evening or afternoon.
sentences.zh: 你最好在你的巅峰时间进行分析性思考，无论是早晨、晚上还是下午。

sentences.en: You're more likely to think in sort of an insightful, creative way during your off-peak hours, when your thinking is a little fuzzy and not so analytical.
sentences.zh: 而在你的非巅峰时间，当思维有点模糊、分析性不强时，你更有可能产生那种富有洞察力的创造性思维。

sentences.en: Also, and I'm not recommending that people drink alcohol, I mean, because there are health repercussions.
sentences.zh: 还有，我并不是建议人们喝酒，毕竟这会对健康产生影响。

sentences.en: But there's plenty of research now that shows that an alcoholic beverage, you know, we're talking just in moderation, it makes your thinking a little fuzzy.
sentences.zh: 但现在有大量研究表明，酒精饮料——当然是指适量饮用——会让你的思维变得有点模糊。

sentences.en: And you can start making these connections that are harder to make if you're more focused and analytical.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能开始建立那些在高度专注和分析状态下难以建立的联系。

sentences.en: Probably one of the most powerful ways to jumpstart creativity is sleep.
sentences.zh: 激发创造力最强大的方法之一可能就是睡眠。

sentences.en: And for three reasons.
sentences.zh: 原因有三。

sentences.en: One, if you sleep, then that puts you in a better mood.
sentences.zh: 首先，如果你睡眠充足，心情会更好。

sentences.en: If you're sleep deprived, you're cranky, you don't feel good.
sentences.zh: 如果你睡眠不足，就会变得暴躁，感觉不适。

sentences.en: But if you get enough sleep, you're in a positive mood, and that helps creativity.
sentences.zh: 但如果你睡眠充足，心情就会积极，这有助于激发创造力。

sentences.en: Sleep also helps with what's called fixation forgetting.
sentences.zh: 睡眠还有助于所谓的“固着遗忘”。

sentences.en: A lot of creativity is blocked because you're focused on a bad idea or bad ideas or non-creative ideas.
sentences.zh: 很多创造力被阻碍，是因为你专注于一个糟糕的想法、一些糟糕的念头，或者非创造性的想法。

sentences.en: When you sleep, and this is the reason why breaks help.
sentences.zh: 当你睡觉时——这也是为什么休息会有帮助的原因。

sentences.en: If you're stuck on something, you take a break, you do fixation forgetting.
sentences.zh: 如果你在某件事上卡住了，休息一下，就能进行“固着遗忘”。

sentences.en: It flushes.
sentences.zh: 它会清除掉这些东西。

sentences.en: You forget the wrong idea that you're stuck on.
sentences.zh: 你会忘记那个让你卡住的错误想法。

sentences.en: Sleep supercharges fixation forgetting and flushes out bad ideas.
sentences.zh: 睡眠能强化“固着遗忘”，清除掉糟糕的想法。

sentences.en: So you can start with more like a blank slate and come up with creative ideas.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能以更像是一张白纸的状态开始，从而想出有创意的点子。

sentences.en: Sleep also promotes what's called memory consolidation.
sentences.zh: 睡眠还能促进所谓的“记忆巩固”。

sentences.en: So the information you take in during the day while you sleep, it becomes consolidated in the brain.
sentences.zh: 所以，你在白天摄入的信息，在睡眠时会在大脑中得到巩固。

sentences.en: And part of that is a reorganization of the knowledge, the information.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分是对知识和信息的重组。

sentences.en: That reorganization can bring out non-obvious ideas, non-obvious features, which is why a lot of people have, they get ideas.
sentences.zh: 这种重组可以引出非显而易见的想法或特征，这就是为什么很多人会突然灵光一现。

sentences.en: Sometimes they wake up in the middle of the night with an idea or the idea presents itself in the morning just as you wake up and you're not fully there yet.
sentences.zh: 有时他们会在半夜醒来时想到一个点子，或者在早晨刚醒、意识还未完全清醒时，点子就自己浮现出来了。

sentences.en: And, for example, Paul McCartney got the melody for the song Yesterday in his sleep.
sentences.zh: 例如，保罗·麦卡特尼就是在睡梦中得到了歌曲《Yesterday》的旋律。

sentences.en: He woke up.
sentences.zh: 他醒了过来。

sentences.en: There it was.
sentences.zh: 旋律就在那里。

sentences.en: He wrote it down.
sentences.zh: 他把它写了下来。

sentences.en: He didn't even know if this melody was something he had come up with or something he'd heard somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 他甚至不知道这旋律是他自己想出来的，还是在别处听到的。

sentences.en: So he ran the tune by John Lennon.
sentences.zh: 于是他把这首曲子弹给约翰·列侬听。

sentences.en: John Lennon said, never heard it before.
sentences.zh: 约翰·列侬说，以前从没听过。

sentences.en: It sounds great.
sentences.zh: 听起来很棒。

sentences.en: He ran it by their manager.
sentences.zh: 他又弹给他们的经纪人听。

sentences.en: The manager said, never heard it before.
sentences.zh: 经纪人说，以前从没听过。

sentences.en: Sounds great.
sentences.zh: 听起来很棒。

sentences.en: So he put words to it.
sentences.zh: 于是他为它填了词。

sentences.en: He said, it must have been my idea, you know, and he wrote it and it was voted as the greatest pop song of the 20th century right there.
sentences.zh: 他说，那一定是我的点子，你知道的，他写下了这首歌，它后来被评为20世纪最伟大的流行歌曲。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 那太神奇了。

sentences.en: So sleep, even a short nap, sleep can supercharge creativity.
sentences.zh: 所以睡眠，哪怕只是小睡一会儿，都能极大地激发创造力。

sentences.en: So those are kind of, you know, that's kind of the more established science.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是目前比较成熟的科学结论。

sentences.en: Looking forward, there's emerging research that suggests that electrical or magnetic brain stimulation may eventually be protocols may be developed that will enhance creativity.
sentences.zh: 展望未来，有一些新兴研究表明，电刺激或磁刺激大脑的方案最终可能会被开发出来，用以增强创造力。

sentences.en: Now, I don't think this will become a practical solution for people in general.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为这不会成为大众的实用解决方案。

sentences.en: Like, you know, oh, I have to come up with an idea for an advertising campaign.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，“噢，我得为一个广告活动想个点子”。

sentences.en: Let me juice my brain with electricity.
sentences.zh: “让我用电刺激一下大脑吧。”

sentences.en: I don't think that's going to become a practical solution, but it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这会成为一种实用的解决方案，但这很有趣。

sentences.en: And there may be some very selected situations in which that might be helpful.
sentences.zh: 在某些非常特定的情况下，这可能会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Another possibility is using drugs to enhance creativity.
sentences.zh: 另一种可能性是使用药物来增强创造力。

sentences.en: You know, since the 1960s, people have been talking about psychedelic drugs, for example, to enhance creativity.
sentences.zh: 你知道，自20世纪60年代以来，人们一直在谈论迷幻药等药物对增强创造力的作用。

sentences.en: And there's been research.
sentences.zh: 也有过相关研究。

sentences.en: Most of it is not very rigorous.
sentences.zh: 但大多数研究并不严谨。

sentences.en: Most of it shouldn't be taken too seriously.
sentences.zh: 大部分都不应被太当真。

sentences.en: But now, starting now, is starting to be some research that looks at the issue, the question of whether psychedelic drugs or other drugs may enhance creativity.
sentences.zh: 但现在，开始出现了一些研究，探讨迷幻药或其他药物是否能增强创造力的问题。

sentences.en: And the jury's out.
sentences.zh: 目前还没有定论。

sentences.en: I do not recommend people use psychedelic drugs.
sentences.zh: 我不建议人们使用迷幻药。

sentences.en: You know, we don't really know what the health implications will be.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们并不真正了解它对健康的影响。

sentences.en: And we don't even know if it'll really help with creativity.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至不知道它是否真的有助于创造力。

sentences.en: It may help people to feel like they're being creative, even if it doesn't help them to actually be creative.
sentences.zh: 它可能让人感觉自己很有创造力，即使实际上并没有帮助。

sentences.en: So we don't really know at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以目前我们还不得而知。

sentences.en: But in the future, I wouldn't be surprised if there was developed a sort of a pharmacology of creativity where that might even be helpful.
sentences.zh: 但在未来，如果能开发出一种关于创造力的药理学，并且确实有所帮助，我也不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Maybe even nutrition, certain foods, chemicals in certain foods may eventually be shown to enhance creativity.
sentences.zh: 也许甚至营养学，某些食物或其中的化学成分，最终也会被证明能增强创造力。

sentences.en: So that's sort of the future.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的未来。

sentences.en: And we don't really know at this point.
sentences.zh: 目前我们还真的不知道。

sentences.en: But the general principle of positive mood, feeling safe and getting a lot of sleep, feeling good, being in an environment where your attention can expand,
sentences.zh: 但总的原则是：保持积极的心情，感到安全，保证充足的睡眠，感觉良好，处于一个能让你的注意力得以扩展的环境中，

sentences.en: we know that can promote insightful creativity.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这能促进洞察力式的创造力。

sentences.en: And the, you know, a little bit of stress, a little bit of anxiety, not too much, because, of course, if you're too stressed and, you know,
sentences.zh: 还有，你知道，一点点压力，一点点焦虑，不要太多，因为当然了，如果你压力太大，你知道的，

sentences.en: you won't be thinking clearly about anything.
sentences.zh: 你就无法清晰地思考任何事情了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But just a little bit of pressure, a little bit of stress promotes more analytical thinking.
sentences.zh: 但只要有一点点压力，一点点紧迫感，就能促进分析性思维。

sentences.en: And the ideal thing, of course, is to sort of be able to alternate between these two things.
sentences.zh: 当然，最理想的状态是在这两种思维模式之间切换。

sentences.en: You know, you in an insightful frame of mind, you generate ideas, then you kind of narrow your focus and you edit it, you evaluate it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你处于洞察力的思维框架中时，你产生想法，然后你缩小焦点，进行编辑和评估。

sentences.en: You can, you know, maybe tweak it, make it better.
sentences.zh: 你可以，你知道，稍微调整一下，让它变得更好。

sentences.en: Maybe you can just throw out your ideas if they're no good.
sentences.zh: 如果想法不好，也许你可以直接抛弃它们。

sentences.en: And then you go back to idea generation and then back to idea analysis.
sentences.zh: 然后你再回到想法生成阶段，再回到想法分析阶段。

sentences.en: That's the ideal thing.
sentences.zh: 那才是最理想的。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's not clear whether people can control or learn to control going back and forth between these two modes of thinking.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，人们是否能控制或学会控制在这两种思维模式之间来回切换，目前还不清楚。

sentences.en: Certainly, a lot of people can naturally swing back and forth.
sentences.zh: 当然，很多人可以自然地来回切换。

sentences.en: And, you know, when they're in a particular frame of mind, they can do a particular type of work.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当他们处于某种特定的思维框架时，他们就能完成特定类型的工作。

sentences.en: When they go to another frame of mind, they can do another another way of thinking, another kind of style.
sentences.zh: 当他们进入另一种思维框架时，他们就能以另一种方式思考，采用另一种风格。

sentences.en: But, you know, it would be great if we can develop a technique to train people to shift back and forth at will.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果我们能开发出一种技术来训练人们随心所欲地来回切换，那就太棒了。

sentences.en: And that would be, you know, that would be fantastic.
sentences.zh: 那将会，你知道，那将会非常美妙。

sentences.en: But that's, I think, a ways off.
sentences.zh: 但我认为那还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: I think you've offered a lot of good advice for people to basically put ourselves in places and positions where we can have more of these aha moments.
sentences.zh: 我想你已经为人们提供了很多好的建议，让我们基本上能把自己置于更容易获得这些“啊哈”时刻的地方和位置。

sentences.en: I hope our listeners have gained some insights from your insights.
sentences.zh: 希望我们的听众能从你的见解中获得一些启发。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天能来参加我们的节目，库尼奥斯博士。
